precepts.point: He fought on the side of the Lord and followed the mighty one, and in the descent of Beth-horon he destroyed them that resisted, that the nations might know all their strength.

precepts.text: Moses called Oshea the son of Nun Jehoshua, the same name again, and sent him with the men to spy out the land of Canaan: to see whether the people were strong or weak, few or many, the cities tents or strongholds, the land fat or lean.
precepts.point: He fought on the side of the Lord and followed the mighty one, and in the descent of Beth-horon he destroyed them that resisted, that the nations might know all their strength.

precepts.point: That all the children of Israel might see that it is good to follow the Lord: his life was put there as the example.

precepts.text: The earth in its youth brought forth greater stature, and each generation since is less than the one before.
precepts.point: They came to the brook of Eshcol and cut down a branch with one cluster of grapes, and bare it between two upon a staff. The cluster was so great it took two men to carry it, for the earth was younger then and brought forth greater stature in its fruit and its men.

note.label: Numbers 13: The Spies Search the Land

precepts.why:
At the brook of Eshcol the spies “cut down from thence a branch with one cluster of grapes, and they bare it between two upon a staff.” One cluster of grapes took two men to carry it. The earth was younger then and brought forth greater stature in its fruit and its men, the children of Anak among them.

Esdras asks the earth why those she brings forth now are “like those that were before, but less of stature”, and she answers: “They that be born in the the strength of youth are of one fashion, and they that are born in the time of age, when the womb faileth, are otherwise.” Then: “Consider thou therefore also, how that ye are less of stature than those that were before you. And so are they that come after you less than ye, as the creatures which now begin to be old, and have passed over the strength of youth.”

The earth in its youth brought forth greater stature, and each generation since is less than the one before. That is why the fruit of the land in the time of the firstripe grapes was of a size no one sees today.

precepts.text: For God hath not given us the spirit of fear; but of power, and of love, and of a sound mind.
precepts.point: The Lord had willed them to go up, but these men were so out of the spirit that they forgot He had already destroyed mightier nations before them. An evil report spreads a spirit of fear, but the Most High has not given His people the spirit of fear.

note.label: Numbers 13: The Spies Search the Land

precepts.why:
Caleb said, “Let us go up at once, and possess it; for we are well able to overcome it.” But the men that went up with him said, “We be not able to go up against the people; for they are stronger than we”, and brought up an evil report, and were in their own sight as grasshoppers.

An evil report spreads a spirit of fear. But “God hath not given us the spirit of fear; but of power, and of love, and of a sound mind.” The Lord had willed them to go up, and these men were so out of the spirit that they forgot He had already destroyed mightier nations before them.

The fear was not from the Most High. What He gives His people is power, love, and a sound mind, and that is the spirit Caleb spoke from.

precepts.text: The giants were men of great stature, famous from the beginning, yet destroyed because they had no wisdom.
precepts.point: The Lord had willed them to go up, but these men were so out of the spirit that they forgot He had already destroyed mightier nations before them. An evil report spreads a spirit of fear, but the Most High has not given His people the spirit of fear.

note.label: Numbers 13: The Spies Search the Land

precepts.why:
The spies said, “there we saw the giants, the sons of Anak, which come of the giants: and we were in our own sight as grasshoppers, and so we were in their sight.” Baruch tells what became of the giants.

“There were the giants famous from the beginning, that were of so great stature, and so expert in war. Those did not the Lord choose, neither gave he the way of knowledge unto them: But they were destroyed, because they had no wisdom, and perished through their own foolishness.”

Men of great stature, famous and expert in war, and the Lord destroyed them anyway, because they had no wisdom. The Lord had already destroyed mightier nations before Israel, and the ten spies forgot it and feared the sons of Anak instead of believing the God who willed them to go up.

precepts.text: By the law of war the fearful were sent back home, lest they put their fear upon the other men.
precepts.point: The Lord had willed them to go up, but these men were so out of the spirit that they forgot He had already destroyed mightier nations before them. An evil report spreads a spirit of fear, but the Most High has not given His people the spirit of fear.

note.label: Numbers 13: The Spies Search the Land

precepts.why:
The evil report of the ten spies spread a spirit of fear through the congregation. The law of war was written for that very thing.

“But as for such as were building houses, or had betrothed wives, or were planting vineyards, or were fearful, those he commanded that they should return, every man to his own house, according to the law.” By the law the fearful were sent back home, lest they put their fear upon the other men.

The ten spies were the fearful men, and instead of going home they stood before all the congregation and put their fear on the whole camp, and Israel was not able to go up.

precepts.text: The men that went up brought an evil report of the land and discouraged the people; that is the history Moses set before Reuben and Gad.
precepts.point: Wherefore discourage ye the heart of the children of Israel from going over into the land which the Lord hath given them: thus did your fathers when they were sent from Kadesh-barnea to see the land. That goes back into the history of the spies in Numbers 13; the fathers were not even in the land yet and were already getting comfortable.

note.label: Numbers 32: The Inheritance of Reuben and Gad on This Side Jordan

precepts.why:
Moses asked Gad and Reuben, “Shall your brethren go to war, and shall ye sit here?” and “wherefore discourage ye the heart of the children of Israel from going over into the land which the Lord hath given them? Thus did your fathers, when I sent them from Kadesh–barnea to see the land.” That goes back into the history of the spies.

“But the men that went up with him said, We be not able to go up against the people; for they are stronger than we. And they brought up an evil report of the land which they had searched unto the children of Israel, saying, The land, through which we have gone to search it, is a land that eateth up the inhabitants thereof; and all the people that we saw in it are men of a great stature. And there we saw the giants, the sons of Anak, which come of the giants: and we were in our own sight as grasshoppers, and so we were in their sight.”

The fathers were not even in the land yet and were already getting comfortable; their evil report discouraged the heart of the children of Israel. That is the history Moses set before Reuben and Gad when they asked to sit on this side Jordan while their brethren went to war.

precepts.text: The spies returned after forty days, and Caleb stilled the people before Moses: let us go up at once and possess it, for we are well able to overcome it.
precepts.point: So Moses sware on that day that the land whereon Caleb's feet had trodden would be his inheritance and his children's for ever, because he wholly followed the Lord.

note.label: Joshua 14: Caleb Wholly Followed the Most High

precepts.why:
Caleb tells Joshua, “Forty years old was I when Moses the servant of the Lord sent me from Kadesh–barnea to espy out the land; and I brought him word again as it was in mine heart.” Here is that word. “And they returned from searching of the land after forty days”, came to Moses, Aaron and all the congregation at Kadesh, “and shewed them the fruit of the land.” The land “floweth with milk and honey”, but “the people be strong that dwell in the land, and the cities are walled, and very great: and moreover we saw the children of Anak there.” The Amalekites in the south, the Hittites, Jebusites and Amorites in the mountains, the Canaanites by the sea and by the coast of Jordan.

Then Caleb: “And Caleb stilled the people before Moses, and said, Let us go up at once, and possess it; for we are well able to overcome it.” That is the word as it was in his heart. Caleb was not playing any games; he was about that business, ready to go and take the land, because he understood the Most High had already promised us the land, so he had no fear. That is the spirit that says, let us go up at once and possess it, and that is what wholly following the Lord looks like.

precepts.text: The men that went up with him brought an evil report of giants, saying we were in our own sight as grasshoppers, and made the people afraid.
precepts.point: So Moses sware on that day that the land whereon Caleb's feet had trodden would be his inheritance and his children's for ever, because he wholly followed the Lord.

note.label: Joshua 14: Caleb Wholly Followed the Most High

precepts.why:
“Nevertheless my brethren that went up with me made the heart of the people melt”. This is how they did it. “But the men that went up with him said, We be not able to go up against the people; for they are stronger than we.” They “brought up an evil report of the land”, calling it “a land that eateth up the inhabitants thereof”, full of “men of a great stature”; “there we saw the giants, the sons of Anak, which come of the giants: and we were in our own sight as grasshoppers, and so we were in their sight.”

The men that went with Caleb brought up an evil report, made the people afraid, and made them doubt. Caleb alone “wholly followed the Lord my God”, and that is why Moses sware that day that the land his feet had trodden would be his inheritance and his children's for ever.

precepts.text: Of the tribe of Ephraim, Oshea the son of Nun: Joshua and his father Nun were of the tribe of Ephraim.
precepts.point: They buried him in the border of his inheritance in Timnathserah, which is in mount Ephraim; he is buried in Ephraim because Joshua was of the tribe of Ephraim, the same tribe as Nun his father.

note.label: Joshua 24: Choose You This Day Whom Ye Will Serve

precepts.why:
They buried Joshua “in the border of his inheritance in Timnath–serah, which is in mount Ephraim”. He is buried in Ephraim because Joshua was of the tribe of Ephraim, the same tribe as Nun his father. That is in the list of the spies: “Of the tribe of Ephraim, Oshea the son of Nun.”

Oshea the son of Nun is Joshua, and his tribe is Ephraim. So his inheritance, and his grave, are in mount Ephraim.

precepts.text: Of the tribe of Ephraim, Oshea the son of Nun; Oshea the son of Nun is Joshua, whom Moses called Jehoshua.
precepts.point: Joshua the son of Nun dies at a hundred and ten years old and is buried in the border of his inheritance in Timnath-heres, in the mount of Ephraim, because Joshua was of the tribe of Ephraim; he was buried in the land of his own tribe's inheritance.

note.label: Judges 2: No League with the Inhabitants of the Land

precepts.why: Joshua was buried “in the border of his inheritance in Timnath–heres, in the mount of Ephraim”. Why Ephraim? Because Joshua was of the tribe of Ephraim. Among the men Moses sent to search the land: “Of the tribe of Ephraim, Oshea the son of Nun.” Oshea the son of Nun is Joshua, whom Moses called Jehoshua. So Joshua the son of Nun, the servant of the Lord, was buried in the land of his own tribe’s inheritance.

points: The Lord spake unto Moses: send thou men, that they may search the land of Canaan, which I give unto the children of Israel. Which I give: the fight was already the Lord's, and the land already given.
The men sent were not regular brothers; every one a ruler among them, heads of the children of Israel, men of renown who could lead other men.

note.label: 70 Times 7: The Perfection of Mercy Through Christ

points: They returned after forty days and agreed the land flowed with milk and honey; then verse 28 turns on one word: nevertheless. The people be strong, the cities are walled, we saw the children of Anak. Doubt entered on the heels of the promise.

note.label: 70 Times 7: The Perfection of Mercy Through Christ

points: Caleb stilled the people and said, Let us go up at once and possess it, for we are well able to overcome it. Caleb showed faith and courage: the Most High already said he would deliver the enemy into our hands, so their stature did not matter.

note.label: 70 Times 7: The Perfection of Mercy Through Christ

points: But the men that went up with him brought an evil report: we were in our own sight as grasshoppers. Rulers and leaders, shook with doubt and fear; and doubt and fear are Satan's playground.

note.label: 70 Times 7: The Perfection of Mercy Through Christ

points: But the men that went up with him said, we be not able to go up against the people, for they are stronger than we. You cannot have men like that in your circle.

note.label: Book of Our Fathers: Who’s Who Part 3

points: The Lord told Moses to send men to search the land of Canaan, one ruler of every tribe of their fathers. Among them were Caleb the son of Jephunneh of the tribe of Judah, and Oshea the son of Nun, whom Moses called Jehoshua, that is Joshua.

note.label: Numbers 13: The Spies Search the Land

points: Sending out spies to learn the landscape, the people, and their strength is the wisdom of war; Moses had learned such things as a leader in Egypt.

note.label: Numbers 13: The Spies Search the Land
